findings.title: Redaction list omits names and addresses that the prompt says must never be repeated
findings.problem: The redaction rule covers only e-mail, phone, card and ID numbers, yet the personal-details rule says names and addresses must never be repeated, so the code path for names and addresses is undefined.
findings.proof: e-mail addresses, phone, card and ID numbers in a message are replaced by placeholders before any model, tool or log sees them
findings.fix: Add names and street addresses to the redaction rule, or state that they are handled only by the model rule and are not redacted by code.

findings.title: No human-oversight or escalation path beyond the store hand-off
findings.problem: Limited-risk recommendation context has no defined route to a human reviewer for complaints, disputed recommendations or model failures; the only escalation is to the store or to professionals.
findings.fix: Add an escalation instruction that names a review channel for disputed or failed recommendations and states how the logged turns are reviewed.

findings.title: No guardrail against manipulative or biased recommendation
findings.problem: The prompt bans paid placement but gives no rule against brand-biased ranking, urgency or pressure wording, or fairness checks across brands, which a recommendation use case under NIST AI RMF needs.
findings.fix: Add a short rule forbidding pressure or urgency language and requiring ranking to follow only the stated constraints and cited evidence, with a fairness check in the evaluation suite.

findings.title: Relaxed filters conflict with the rule that hard constraints must never change
findings.problem: The search tool silently loosens budget and age filters when too few products match, while the Retriever rule forbids changing hard constraints; the prompt does not say whether relaxed results may be shown.
findings.proof: If too few products meet every filter the tool loosens them in a fixed order and says which in `relaxed`
findings.fix: State in the Retriever rule that any result from a relaxed search must carry a caveat for the relaxed budget or age, or must be dropped, and that relaxed results never count as meeting the stated constraint.

findings.title: Retriever constraint rule clashes with tool-side loosening
findings.problem: The Retriever is told never to drop or change hard constraints, but the tool it calls is designed to drop them under a fixed order that the prompt never defines.
findings.proof: Never drop or change the shopper's hard constraints, never repeat a call, and make no call for a declined part of the message.
findings.fix: Reconcile the two by stating which filters the tool may loosen and that the Answerer must caveat every such result.

findings.title: Category lists conflict between the tool description and the catalog file
findings.problem: The tool schema lists different largest categories from the catalog file, so the model receives two inconsistent descriptions of the same catalog.
findings.proof: Largest categories: Toys & Games (6,521), Home & Kitchen (688), Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry (628)
findings.fix: Keep one authoritative category list and reference it from the other file instead of restating it with different values.

findings.title: Tool description omits the relaxation order it depends on
findings.problem: The rag.search description says filters are loosened in a fixed order but never lists that order, so the model cannot predict which constraint will be dropped.
findings.fix: Add the fixed relaxation order to the rag.search description, or return the dropped filter names in the relaxed field only.

findings.title: Best-fit ranking is not operationalised
findings.problem: The prompt requires the best fit to come first but defines no criteria for fit, so ordering rests on the model's judgment rather than on the evidence.
findings.proof: The best fit to the request and its stated limits comes first; no placement is paid for.
findings.fix: Define fit as a count of satisfied hard constraints followed by evidence match, and require the Answerer to name the constraint that placed each item first.

findings.title: Untrusted-content protection depends on an unspecified server filter
findings.problem: Injection resistance relies on the MCP server stripping instruction-like text, a heuristic the prompt does not describe, and the Answerer and Critic prompts do not restate the data-only rule.
findings.proof: the MCP server removes instruction-like text from them before any model sees it
findings.fix: Restate the data-only fencing rule in the Answerer and Critic prompts and document what the server filter does and does not catch.

findings.title: Release-gate rule sits in the runtime prompt
findings.problem: The release and governance-gate rule is a build-time process requirement placed in the runtime operating prompt, where it adds tokens without changing agent behaviour.
findings.proof: Release rule: a version ships only when the test suite and a ProofAgent run of the project's scenarios pass the governance gate
findings.fix: Move the release rule to the project's release documentation and keep the runtime prompt limited to agent behaviour.

findings.title: Knowledge file restates the system prompt's grounding rule
findings.problem: scope_and_policy.md repeats the grounding and citation rules already stated in the system prompt and the Answerer and Critic prompts.
findings.proof: It never states a price, rating, availability or product property that is not in a tool result of the conversation
findings.fix: Delete the restated grounding and citation bullets from scope_and_policy.md and keep one canonical rule in the system prompt.

findings.title: Catalog file repeats the no-ratings rule already in the schema and prompt
findings.problem: catalog_and_sources.md restates the no-ratings and no-availability rules that appear in the system prompt and in the rag.search description.
findings.proof: The catalog has **no customer ratings and no review counts**.
findings.fix: Remove the duplicated rating and availability bullets from the catalog file and rely on the single rule in the system prompt.

context_engineering.summary: The context is strongly engineered for grounding, injection separation and fixed-sentence safety, but it repeats its rules across the system prompt and knowledge files, leaves a few gaps in redaction and escalation, and has conflicts in constraint relaxation and category lists.
